packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-01 - unverified image reading (UTF-8)

Exposure note: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this record. The only external labels seen are the pencil shelfmarks written on the photographed leaves themselves ("Stams, STA, Frg. 11_2u" and "Stams, STA, Frg. 11_1u" as I read them on image-001).

Procedure note (beyond the literal rules): the script on the first face is mirror-reversed (see survey). To read it I made horizontally flipped copies of the packet tiles (sips --flip horizontal) in a scratch directory and read from those. Line numbers below are counted from the top of each tile; left/right positions refer to the FLIPPED (readable) orientation unless stated.

LAYOUT SURVEY - face 1 (overview image-001)
- Two separate leaves (or the two halves of a split bifolium) photographed side by side on black, colour chart and mm scale present. Left piece labelled in pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 11_2u", right piece "... 11_1u".
- The ink writing on both pieces is mirror-reversed: letters read right-to-left and are reversed in shape. Observation: the ink is brownish and fairly even; this looks like an offset (ink transferred from a facing written sheet) or writing seen in reverse, not text written on this surface the normal way. Interpretation only.
- Left piece: single block of long lines, c. 35 lines, in a fast German-type cursive (documentary/chancery cursive, not book hand). At top right a large black bold word in mirrored gothic/textura-like letters that reads (when flipped) roughly "rannal"/"lannoer"?? - a heading or a printed/offset word. Between left piece and right piece, along the right edge of the left piece, a narrow strip with small printed (typeset) text, also mirror-reversed (letters like "bit", "ncia", "ti", "ca"): a stub of a printed leaf, probably a binding strip.
- Right piece: single block of long lines, c. 33 lines, same cursive, damaged at upper left (loss, notch) and lower right.
- Lower parts of both pieces: blank-ish areas with scattered faint brownish cursive notes, several short lines in a lighter ink, some appearing to be signatures/marks with a flourished capital K-like sign (e.g. "...g K") - these too appear mirror-reversed. Pen-trial-like strokes.
- No columns, no rubrics, no ruling visible; no enlarged initials apart from capitals in the cursive. Running text of a document/letter/protocol type (observation of form only).

LAYOUT SURVEY - face 2 (overview image-014)
- Same two pieces, other side; pencil labels "Stams, STA, Frg. 11_2v" (left) and "Stams, STA, Frg. 11_1v" (right) as I read them. Note the left/right order: on this face the 11_2 piece is on the left again.
- Both surfaces are covered with brown paste/glue with strong brush-stroke marks; essentially no handwriting on the main areas. Scattered isolated coloured marks: blue and red letter-like shapes (e.g. a blue and a red "C"/"G"-like loop on the left piece, a blue loop, a red mark and a blue "H"/"I"-like form on the right piece). Observation: these look like offsets or show-through of coloured printed/painted initials or paragraph marks, not text on this face. Interpretation only.
- Left piece top: a strip of paper with faint brown cursive flourishes (a few words) and some greenish colour.
- Right piece, right edge: a narrow strip of a printed leaf (typeset gothic type, black), legible in correct orientation, c. 18 visible short line-ends/line-beginnings, set vertically along the edge. A printed strip also runs along the top edge of the right piece (illegible at overview scale).
- Faint traces of printed type show through at the lower left of the left piece (mirror/show-through).

LAYOUT SURVEY - image-027 (third overview)
- The same face-2 pieces rotated 90 degrees so that the printed strip on piece 11_1 runs horizontally at the top (the 11_1 piece is the upper one, 11_2 the lower). Printed strip: two columns of gothic type, c. 4 lines visible, with a red mark between columns; left column partly lost/obscured. Red and blue offset marks on the pasted surfaces as before. Tiles image-028 and image-029 are presumably the left and right halves of that strip area.

=====================================================================
FACE 2 PRINTED STRIP - image-028 (left half of the strip shown in image-027)
=====================================================================
Observation: the strip holds two areas of gothic type.
(a) Left area (x c. 280-940): pale grey type that reads MIRROR-REVERSED in the tile, i.e. show-through or offset of type from the other side / another layer. Two bold black capitals ("D" on line 2 and "G" on line 3 in tile orientation) and a red stroke ("I"/paragraph mark) above them are upright and dark, i.e. on this surface. I made a horizontally flipped, contrast-stretched crop (scratchpad p01/028_left_flipH.jpg) to read the grey type. Lines of grey type, counted from top of strip:
 028 a1  [illegible traces] ... s(?)iditenr(?) | (perhaps "...diterur" / "...ditur"; end of a word in -tur? uncertain)
 028 a2  ...m oztiado(?) laudat(ur?)   ("ozt-" could be "orti-"/"ora-"; I cannot settle it; reading "orando"? only as a guess)
 028 a3  ...mlt(?) : detrimentum
Note: line a3 begins (in flipped view) with "...mlt :" preceded by the black "G"/"S" capital which belongs to the near surface, not to the grey line.
(b) Near-surface black type in tile orientation (upright), at x c. 790-920:
 028 b1  [red "I"-like stroke, rubric/paragraph mark]
 028 b2  D [bold capital] m (?) - "Dm" or "D" + traces
 028 b3  lm:G (?)  - read in tile orientation "lm:G" with bold capital; may be part of the mirrored line rather than separate; uncertain.
(c) Right edge of tile, x c. 1000-1210, upright black type, start of the right column (continues on image-029):
 028 c1  ler
 028 c2  (paragraph sign/"²"-like mark) per
 028 c3  passion

=====================================================================
FACE 2 PRINTED STRIP - image-029 (right half; overlaps image-028 at "ler/per/passion")
=====================================================================
Upright black gothic type (rotunda-like, long s, round r after o), single column of c. 5 lines; middle of lines 3-5 obscured by pale mirror-reversed show-through and a loss. Line numbers from top of the printed block:
 029 l1  [traces] ... (?)tonis(?)            (only the top of the letters; "-tonis"/"-conis" uncertain)
 029 l2  [illegible] ... a tredecio ca
 029 l3  ler[illegible, show-through] ...  (t)empore seuissima   ("ſeuiſſima"; first letter long s; = saevissima?)  - the "t" of tempore lost, "empore" clear
 029 l4  (mark) per[illegible] ageba[...] sub decio . Et post
 029 l5  passionem beati [illegible 1-2 letters, damage] ii post tertiam diem
Notes: "ler" (l3) and "per" (l4) and "passionem" (l5) are line-beginnings of the same column; "a tredecio ca" (l2) is a line-end, so the line-beginning of l2 is lost. Between "ageba" and "sub" a loss/partial letter ("[t]"?). After "beati" a small damaged gap then "ii" / "n"(?). Lines 3-4 middle: pale mirrored type show-through, not read.
Same overlap: 028 c1-c3 = 029 l3-l5 beginnings.

=====================================================================
FACE 1 - CURSIVE TEXT (mirror-reversed on the leaf; read from flipped tiles)
=====================================================================
Mapping: face-1 tiles are a 4 x 3 grid (002-005 top row, 006-009 middle, 010-013 bottom), columns left-to-right in the original photo. After horizontal flipping the column order reverses: flip-005/009/013 show the LEFT (line-beginning) half of piece 11_1u, flip-004/008/012 its right half; flip-003/007/011 the left half of piece 11_2u and flip-002/006/010 its right half. In readable orientation, therefore, piece 11_1u comes first (left) and 11_2u second (right). Which piece precedes in the text is not established.
Script: German documentary cursive (Kurrent type), long s, looped d, h with descender, "vnd" with v, "ai" spellings (gerechtigkait, gemain, allain). Language German. Comma-like virgules/commas used as punctuation. Line numbers count from the top of each tile.

--- flip-005 (piece 11_1u, left half, top third; line-beginnings) ---
 005.01  geschen(?) , der herrn [h]erzog(?)[...]                         (first word uncertain: "geschehen"/"gesehen"?)
 005.02  [a]m(b)tgericht(?) [C/S]...ing[...] ma[...]ch(?) [...]           (very uncertain)
 005.03  Johannsen Abbte . vnd Capitel(?)[...]
 005.04  [...]hochsten(?) ordenlichen Grundtherrn(?) vnd
 005.05  vnd gerechtigkait , ob gemainen [...]
 005.06  [...]en / ain Zechofen(?) , am ort(?) , thu(?)n [...]           ("Zechofen"/"Zehofen" uncertain)
 005.07  der glogen(?) , allain gert(?) die gemain [...]
 005.08  [...] Hofl(?) . Weder(?) Recht(?) Fron(?)schmadem(?)[...]       (largely uncertain)
 005.09  die Eggennuß(?) , das drit Tramstl(?) [...]
 005.10  Ihr weisen(?) , Gärten vnd Städl(?) , [...]
 005.11  anstöß , ob die wasser rhinnen(?) , [...]
 005.12  Ich obgemelter [name, illegible: "Cristo..."?] [initial] [...]   (line indented: new paragraph)
 005.13  [...]zemen(?) aufgezaichent(?) [...] ainmütig(?) , ob [...]
 005.14  [...]ung(?) Volco(?) [...]olt(?) , Zaigen oder an[...]
 005.15  [...]ra(?) nicht hinwegwenden(?) , auch die[...]
 005.16  [tops of letters only]
Note: paler, thinner mirror-reversed writing also visible at right of this tile (a second, fainter layer of offset in the reverse sense); not read.

--- flip-004 (piece 11_1u, right half, top third; continues the lines of flip-005; overlap of c. 1-2 words at the left edge) ---
 004.01  [...]lichen(?) [...] herrsch[aft?](?) [...] | (faint, line badly worn)
 004.02  [...] Sigler(?) [...] vnd all[...] hieuor(?) [...]
 004.03  [...]m(?)men Prelaten(?) das [...]
 004.04  [...]herrn vnd Castner(?) [...]                       (overlaps 005.04 "Grundtherrn(?)")
 004.05  [...]en Gmain(?) [...] / [...] selbs(?) auf der
 004.06  [...]farn(?) [...] Wässern(?) / an [...]
 004.07  gemain Landstraß(?) [...]en mitten
 004.08  [...]mädern samt ainer Kä(s)er(?) [...]               (continues 005.08 "...schmädern"?)
 004.09  [...]stl(?) , das viert Vnnder(?) Stue(?)[...]        (continues 005.09 "das drit ..."; so a numbered list "das drit ... das viert ...")
 004.10  [...]Städl(?) , [...]ningen(?) [...] vnd [...]
 004.11  [...]n verwenden(?) , Innhalt vnd [...]
 004.12  [...] herrlande(?)[...] , [...] Kirch : vnd [...]
 004.13  [...] ob gemeiß(?) hab(?) mit de[m] selb[en]
 004.14  oder ainicher(?) nachkommen(?) [...]
 004.15  auch dieselben zu [...] [...]
Notes: A second, paler mirrored writing layer crosses this tile (diagonal loops), not read. Brown spot near top centre. Many words here are uncertain; the clear spans are 004.07, 004.08 ("samt ainer"), 004.09 ("das viert"), 004.13-004.15.

--- flip-009 (piece 11_1u, left half, middle third; line-beginnings) ---
Overlap: 009.01-009.04 = 005.12-005.15 (same lines, not new text). New lines from 009.05:
 009.05  [...]t vnnd Gu(e)ter(?) ze verschaffen [...]          ("Gueter"/"Gwalter" uncertain; "ze verschaffen" fairly clear)
 009.06  [...]b ain Pfundt pf(enning)(?) [...] geben(?) [...]   (abbreviated money term after "Pfundt"; uncertain)
 009.07  [...]ire Krafft(?) . verschwainung(?) [...]
 009.08  bewilligung gemelter grundtherrn(?) [...]
 009.09  [...]: Hauslewten , ist ausgeschlossen , [...]
 009.10  [...]ollten(?) gemainen obenmelten(?)[...]
 009.11  [A]bstellung(?) ewiglichen vnd be[...]
 009.12  [...] vnd aufzuweisen , wann wie dann
 009.13  Grundtherrn zuthun pflichtig sein
 009.14  [...]als Hauslewten wider das gemain [...]
 009.15  [...]tl(?) [...] ... [...] Iabrt(?) [...] [...]           (heavily worn)
 009.16  [...]t [...] [...] [...]laiß(?) erkennen(?) . [...]
 009.17  [...] [...] gehaimst(?) hat , das [...]
 009.18  [...]wand(?) . vnd [...] [...]
Notes: lines 009.15-009.18 are faint and crossed by pale second-layer loops; readings very insecure.

--- flip-008 (piece 11_1u, right half, middle third; continues flip-009 lines) ---
Overlap: 008.01-008.04 = 004.12-004.15 (same lines). Reading here is clearer, so I refine those line-ends:
 008.02  [...] ob gemeiß(?) hab(?) mit derselb[en]            (= 004.13)
 008.03  oder ainicherer(?) nachkhomen[...]                  (= 004.14)
 008.04  [...]ch dieselben zu st[...]en(?) [...] genanndt[...]  (= 004.15; "zu st..len"? uncertain)
New lines (continuing 009.05ff. at the left):
 008.05  [...]n Ir(?) wolten , [...] [...] vnnderhalb(?)/[...]malls(?)
 008.06  [...] dann Iemandt anndern , erfolgen
 008.07  [...] mit der Gerecht[igkait](?) , vom [...]ansetzt(?)
 008.08  [...]ndtherrschafft verschaffen , vnd geben          (= "[Gru]ndtherrschafft")
 008.09  [...]en , sonnder der Grundtherrschafft
 008.10  [...]hab , mit derselben zugehörung(?) , sollen
 008.11  vnd besonnder aines Iedem(?) Iarlichen(?)/Jarbrgen(?) [...]
 008.12  [...] dann [...] die gemainst(?) vnd Lanndtrecht
 008.13  [...]stig sein [...] [...] wider(?) [...] nie(?) abwendt(?)
 008.14  [...]gemain [...] Tirollisch(?) Lanndtrecht mit
 008.15  [...] ordenlich(?) vnd vngeuarlich(?) , der
 008.16  [...] [...] [...]erben(?) . [...]
 008.17  [...] [...] [...]amb(?) Sigl(?) hat(?) [...] [...]
 008.18  [...] [...] Gericht(?) [...]herrn(?) [...]
Notes: "Lanndtrecht" (008.12, 008.14) and "Grundtherrschafft" (008.08-09) are among the clearest words on the face. Pale second-layer loops cross lines 008.10-008.18.

--- flip-013 (piece 11_1u, left half, bottom third) ---
Overlap: 013.01-013.03 = 009.16-009.18. Last line of the main text block:
 013.01  [...]t [...] [...]laiß erkennen . [...]            (= 009.16)
